subject: Package options for observability add-ons (retention / tracing / dashboards)
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@acmeretail.com>
To: dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Options for observability add-ons — retention & tracing

Hi Dev,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the runtime performance and the dashboard UX. Procurement and engineering want to better understand how you price the observability add-ons (retention, tracing, advanced dashboards) so we can model cost against our Q1 roadmap. A few specifics: 

- Retention: we need visibility into 3 different buckets — 90 days for hot logs, 365 days foraudited events, and an archival option. Is that a simple tiered SKU or metered?
- Tracing: how do you charge for sampling vs full-span capture? Are there volume discounts at 50M spans/month?
- Dashboards: we have 10 power users today but expect to grow — is seat-based licensing required or can dashboards be metered by dashboard views/queries?
- Discounts & commits: what level of annual commit is needed to get meaningful discounts? We have a limited budget but want to commit if the model scales predictably.

Can you send a short matrix with a few example scenarios (pilot 3 months, annual commit, and a conservative 12-month forecast)? We prefer a one-pager + SOW to move to legal.

Thanks,
Samir Shah
Head of Procurement, Acme Retail
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@acmeretail.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-01T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Options for observability add-ons — retention & tracing

Samir — great to hear the demo landed well. Attached is a concise pricing matrix and a draft SOW to get legal started (attachments: observability_pricing_v2.pdf, SOW-draft.docx). High-level notes up front: 

- Retention SKU: We offer three retention SKUs (30/90/365). Pricing model supports either flat tier (monthly per-GB for that retention bracket) or metered overage (per-GB beyond commit). For your use-case, a hybrid works: commit to a 90-day baseline and enable 365-day archival as an add-on archive tier. 
- Tracing: Default is sampled traces at no extra charge (configurable sampling rate). Full-span capture is an add-on priced per-million spans ingested. At 50M spans/month we can tier to reduce unit cost; see scenario table p.2 of the PDF. 
- Dashboards: We support both seat-based power-user licenses and metered dashboards for casual viewers. For 10 power users + 50 viewers, the mixed model is usually lowest-cost.
- Discounts: Our list discounts scale with committed ARR. Example anchors in the matrix: 12-month commit (5%–12%), 24-month (10%–18%), and strategic (20%+ on case-by-case). Bundling retention + tracing + dashboard seats yields additional crediting.

Proposed next steps: 30-min commercial call to walk the matrix and pick a pilot configuration (I can host Wed 11/3 or Thu 11/4). If you like, Kimberly (CC) will confirm the discount path once we agree ballpark usage numbers.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: observability_pricing_v2.pdf (1p summary + scenarios), SOW-draft.docx (boilerplate)
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, k.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-01T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Options for observability add-ons — retention & tracing

Kimberly / Karthik — forwarding Samir's ask and the materials I just sent. Key commercial points for negotiation: 

- Their ask: flexible retention (90/365/archival), 50M spans/mo sensitivity, and 10 power dashboards today. Budget conscious but willing to commit if the economics work.

My thinking / options: 
- Pilot path (low risk): 3-month pilot with 90-day retention + sampled traces (no full-span). Offer 15% off list for pilot plus a one-time $10k onboarding credit. If they convert to a 12-month commit within 60 days of pilot end, roll pilot fees into commit and provide an additional 5% uplift credit.
- Annual commit path: For a 12-month commit at expected usage (we estimated in the matrix ~ $240k ARR for retention + tracing + 10 seats), propose 12% discount plus bundled credit equivalent to 2 months free applied prorata for year 1.
- Tradeoffs to consider: reduce retention to 180 days instead of 365 to get to a much lower price point — present as TCO tradeoff to the customer. Also can cap full-span capture by percentage of services to avoid runaway cost.

Questions for you: 
1) Is 15% + $10k onboarding credit too aggressive for a first-time pilot (we'd prefer to keep concession under 20% total)?
2) Legal: SOW includes a standard retention SLA clause and export rights; is the SOW-draft language acceptable re: data export / archival responsibilities?
3) Should we offer a fixed dashboard seat bucket vs metered model for clarity in procurement? My recommendation: seat bucket for power users + metered viewers.

FYI — below is Samir's original email snippet for context: 

> On 2026-11-01 09:14, Samir Shah <samir.shah@acmeretail.com> wrote:
> > Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the runtime performance and the dashboard UX. Procurement and engineering want to better understand how you price the observability add-ons...

I'll hold off on the call booking until we align on a concession strategy.

— Dev
From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@acmeretail.com>
To: dev.patel@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmeretail.com
Date: 2026-11-02T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Options for observability add-ons — retention & tracing

Dev — thanks for the quick turnaround and the packet. We reviewed the scenarios with engineering and procurement this morning. A couple of clarifications and a counter-proposal: 

- Pilot: we're happy to run the 3-month pilot with 90-day retention and sampled traces, but procurement needs a modest commercial concession. Can you do 15% off list for the pilot instead of 15% + $10k credit? That keeps our internal approvals simpler.
- Annual commit: if we move to a 12-month commit after pilot, we'd like to see a 15% discount guaranteed (instead of the 12% anchor).
- Dashboards: procurement prefers a seat bucket for power users (10 seats) + 1000 metered viewer-hours/month for the broader team. Please confirm that viewer-hours are supported.

If you can confirm the pilot discount and the viewer-hours metric, we can route the SOW to legal. Also, please send a DocuSign-ready SOW with the pilot appended as a short addendum so we can sign quickly.

Samir Shah
Head of Procurement, Acme Retail

P.S. We prefer DocuSign rather than email signatures — I requested a DocuSign link from our side; if you can mirror that we'll coordinate sign-off tightly.
